subject: Pioneer Retail — Renewal proposal & capacity overlay

From: Samuel Gross <samuel.gross@pioneerretail.com>

Date: 2026-10-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal & Capacity for Pioneer Retail — Oct 26

Hi Irene,

We’re starting budget planning for calendar 2027 and want to lock renewal terms for Pioneer Retail (current term expires 2027-01-31). Traffic has been higher than expected this year — we’re forecasting a 1.8x increase in embed/call volume during Q1.

Two asks from our side:
- Price stability: can you hold current per-token rates for at least the first 6 months post-renewal?
- Capacity overlay: we’d like an option to increase committed capacity by 40% with predictable overage pricing.

I attached our internal renewal request (see Pioneer_Renewal_Request_2026.pdf). Can we schedule a 30-min call next week to walk through options? Procurement (cc’d below) will need a timeline for PO.

Thanks — Sam

Samuel Gross

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-10-27T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal & Capacity for Pioneer Retail — options

Irene / David — drafted two clean options for Pioneer based on usage patterns and the 1.8x Q1 forecast. Attached term_sheet_v2.pdf with line items. Short summary below.

Option A — Staged Commit (recommended if Pioneer wants low unit cost):
- Year 1 commit: +40% tokens vs current (annualized)
- Pricing: 12% discount vs current list on committed units
- True-up quarterly; burst overage at current list + 10% cap for first 90 days
- Upfront obligation: 60% of Year 1 commit billed at signature
- Onboarding credit: $30k to cover migration and integration work

Option B — Temporary Rate Guard + Lower Commit (recommended if they prefer flexibility):
- Year 1 commit: +15% tokens
- Temporary rate guard: current per-token rate held for 6 months post-renewal; thereafter revert to standard list unless commit increased
- Onboarding credit: $15k; burst overage at list price (no cap)

Operational notes:
- Both options require SOC2 evidence (they asked for this historically) — attach SOC2 snapshot.
- We can offer a hybrid: anchor a temporary rate guard for first 3 months and then transition to staged commit with a 6% step discount.

If Pioneer prefers Option B, we should ask for a signed PO by 11/10 to lock Q1 onboarding dates.

—Marissa
Senior Manager, Commercial Programs
Redwood Inference

Proposed hybrid (what we’d like to offer):
- Q1: Temporary rate guard — hold current per-token rates for 3 months post signature.
- Immediately after Q1: transition to a staged commit equal to +30% year-over-year with a 9% discount on committed units.
- Onboarding credit: $25k applied to first invoice.
- 90-day cap on overage pricing at list + 8% while they ramp to committed throughput.

Please confirm if this pathway is acceptable and whether procurement needs a PO by 11/10. If so, we’ll prepare an amendment and DocuSign packet.

Best regards,
Irene

From: Samuel Gross <samuel.gross@pioneerretail.com>

Cc: procurement@pioneerretail.com, finance@pioneerretail.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal options for Pioneer — draft proposal

Irene — appreciate the quick turnaround. The hybrid is close to what we need, but procurement and finance are pushing for stronger protection in Q1 if we commit more later. Two asks from our side:
1) Can you extend the rate guard to 4 months (instead of 3)? That gives us runway to validate traffic and avoid surprises for our merchants.
2) Can you front-load more of the onboarding credit against the first invoice (we’d like $35k applied up front if possible).

Also — PO timeline: procurement needs a final amendment and a line-itemed invoice by 11/12 to route through internal approvals. If you can get that to us, we can likely sign and issue a PO before 11/20.

Thanks — Sam

Samuel Gross
Head of Platform Engineering
Pioneer Retail
